text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency spike on streaming-infer (region: us-west-2). Metric threshold breached: p99 > 2.5s for 5m. Auto-escalation to oncall.

ops-bot: Affected model variants: redwood-open-int8-v3 (recent quant profile: qv3). Observed: streaming stalls, KV-cache miss rate up, tail tokens stalling.

irene-oncall: on it. paging now. assigning severity: Sev2 for production SLO breach.

alex: ack. pulling graphs. which tenants impacted?

sam: quick look — traffic map shows 12% of streaming requests hitting int8 path, p95 from 180ms -> 820ms, p99 from 1.1s -> 3.2s in last 7m.

priya: @sam can you grab the recent rollout diff? I want to confirm qv3 was the only change in the last deploy window.

sam: grabbing diff... found: deploy 2002103600 pushed quant profile qv3 to canary->prod, rollout batch size 30% -> 100% over 2h.

mateo: customer-impact check: preliminary list: "acme-payments" and "edu-labs" show elevated latency in traces. CS pinged.

jill-cs: pinged both customers, they reported timeouts on long streaming responses. They've opened tickets. I'm drafting a status note.

irene-oncall: tl;dr hypothesis: qv3 quant profile increases dequant KV churn for longer contexts causing streaming stalls for some sequences. Need safe mitigation: route affected traffic to fp16 variant and rollback qv3.

alex: agree. mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout (if still running) 2) route canary & prod traffic for streaming-infer to redwood-open-fp16-v1 fallback 3) rollback qv3 from modelstore or apply hotfix config to force older profile 4) monitor p95/p99 and streaming token stalls.

priya: ops: can we toggle routing rule quickly? command below to flip route via traffic-router service:

```
curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/route/streaming-infer -d '{"override":"redwood-open-fp16-v1","scope":"prod","reason":"latency spike qv3"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN"
```
sam: running the toggle now. watching metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy 2002103600 -> paused by priya at 2002104145. Rollout freeze applied.

sam: router response OK. new route applied, ~40% traffic diverted to fp16 in first 30s.

irene-oncall: also escalate to runtime if KV-cache eviction is the root cause — @alex can you check the serving logs for LRU churn or de-serialization errors?

alex: tailing serving logs on node gpt-srv-12: seeing repeated flushes of KV cache for model redwood-open-int8-v3 around 2002104000..2002104020. Logs: `kv_cache->evict(key=prefix:session:xxxx, reason=capacity)` and occasional `dequant-fail` warnings.

sam: interesting — dequant-fail suggests path mismatch between kernel and quant layout. Could be qv3 produced tensors incompatible with fast-dequant path under certain sequence lengths.

mateo: what about fallback? Is fp16 stable under same load?

sam: fp16 path latency stable: p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 540ms. No streaming stalls observed.

irene-oncall: good. continue diversion to fp16 for full prod while we roll back qv3. Priya, can you trigger modelstore rollback?

priya: initiating rollback command to restore qv2 profile:

```
./modelstore rollback --model redwood-open-int8 --profile qv2 --env prod --reason "latency spike qv3"
```
deploy-bot: rollback job 2002104205 started. progress: 0% -> 60% -> 100%.

priya: rollback completed. modelstore now serving qv2 for int8 variant. Confirmed on control plane.

sam: metrics starting to show improvement — p99 trending down. p99 at 3m after rollback: 1.2s -> 0.7s. Streaming stalls decreased by ~85%.

irene-oncall: good. keep routes to fp16 until we have steady-state p99 < 600ms for 15m. Also schedule postmortem: root-cause to cover quant profiling tests not catching this sequence-length KV churn.

jill-cs: updated customers: short status: "We've applied a mitigation routing to a stable FP16 variant and rolled back the recent quant profile. We expect normal latency to return shortly. We'll follow up with postmortem." They acknowledged.

alex: action items: - runtime team to add dequant compatibility checks to CI - infra to add KV-cache churn alerting threshold - product to add canary ramp guard on quant profile rollouts (max 30% until 24h)

irene-oncall: assigning owners: runtime -> @sam, infra -> @mateo, product -> @priya. I'll keep incident open for monitoring until 15m stable window.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: p99 recovered to 430ms (last 5m). No customer errors reported in last 10m. Incident ticket: INC-2002106789 created.

irene-oncall: thanks everyone. leaving a short blameless note in incident tracker and will run full blameless postmortem in the next 48h. If new regressions appear, re-open.

alex: leaving handoff notes for next oncall: summary, mitigation, owners, links to logs and modelstore rollback id 2002104205.

priya: +1, adding follow-up tasks to triage board.

jill-cs: will follow up with customers once postmortem has actionable timeline.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: SLOs back within target. Case closed pending postmortem."
